q: 1. The unit of measurement for concrete work in R.C.C. is
explain: Major concrete works, including Reinforced Cement Concrete (RCC), are calculated by volume in cubic meters.

q: 2. The unit of measurement for beading provided in door and window frame, rafters etc. is
explain: Beading and thin decorative strips are measured in linear units (running meters).

q: 3. The unit of measurement of electric wire (diameter specified) is
explain: Electric wire is a linear item, so once its diameter/gauge is specified, its quantity is measured by running length, i.e., per metre.

q: 4. The quantity of wood of the shutters of doors and windows is calculated in
explain: Door and window shutters are thin flat panels, so their quantity is measured in square meters (area) rather than volume.

q: 5. Following items of earth work is not measured separately
explain: Preliminary tasks like setting out, clearing small vegetation, and leaving 'dead men' (earth tell-tales) are considered incidental to the main excavation.

q: 6. The quantity of damp proof course (D.P.C) is worked out in
explain: DPC is a thin horizontal layer, so it is measured in square meters.

q: 7. The unit of measurement of plantation of tree (diameter and type specified) is
explain: Tree plantation, once the type/girth is specified, is treated as a linear/count-based item measured per metre (per running metre or spacing basis) in this context.

q: 8. *Scaffolding is calculated in
explain: According to the key, scaffolding is calculated in Sq meters (m^2).

q: 9. Whenever colour washing on a.c.. corrugated sheets is done, in the estimation the plane area of the sheets is increased by
explain: For colour washing on A.C. (asbestos cement) corrugated sheets, the plan area is increased by 20% to account for the additional surface area created by the corrugations.

q: 10. The unit weight of RCC in kg/m³ is
explain: The standard unit weight (density) of reinforced cement concrete used in design and estimation is 2400 kg/m³.

q: 11. *The volume of C.A required to make 100 m^3 of 1:2:4 concrete is
explain: Due to voids and shrinkage, roughly 150-154 m^3 of dry material is needed for 100 m^3 wet concrete. For a 1:2:4 mix, coarse aggregate is 4/7 of that dry volume.

q: 12. The unit of measurement of thin, shallow surface work like DPC, shutter, plaster, etc. is
explain: Thin surface treatments like DPC, shuttering, and plaster have negligible thickness compared to their area, so they are measured in square metres.

q: 13. How many kilo-liters are there in one cubic meter
explain: One cubic meter equals 1000 liters, which equals exactly 1 kilolitre (1 kL = 1000 L).

q: 14. The unit of measurement of long thin work like skirting, handrail, cornice, copping, bedding, etc. is
explain: Long, thin, narrow-section items such as skirting, handrails, cornices, and coping are measured along their length, i.e., per running metre.

q: 15. The quantity of cement required for 1 m^3 plaster C:S(1:5) ratio
explain: Calculating dry mortar volume and cement portion results in approximately 310 kg.

q: 16. The weight of 10 mm diameter mild steel rod per metre length is equal to
explain: Using the standard formula W = d²/162 kg/m for mild steel bars, a 10 mm bar gives 100/162 ≈ 0.617 kg/m, i.e., approximately 0.62 kg/m.

q: 17. The unit of supply of ordinary cement bag
explain: Cement bags are discrete countable units, so they are supplied and priced by number (no.) of bags, each bag being a standard 50 kg.

q: 18. The volume of cement required to prepare 100 cubic metre of 1 : 2 : 4 concrete is
explain: Dry volume = 154 m^3. Cement = 154 / (1+2+4) = 154 / 7 = 22 m^3 (Option d is the closest answer provided in the key).

q: 19. One dharmi is equivalent to
explain: A 'dharmi' is a local unit of measurement, standardly taken as 2.40 kg in this context.

q: 20. The weight of 12mm diameter mild steel per meter length is equal to
21. How many kilo-liters are in one cubic meter?
explain: 1 m^3 = 1000 liters. Since 1000 liters = 1 kilo-liter, 1 m^3 = 1 kL.

q: 22. The area of the cross-section of a road fully in banking, is
explain: For a road fully in banking with ground cross slope, the standard derived formula for cross-sectional area is [sb^2 + r^2(2bd+Sd)^2] / (r^2 - S^2).

q: 23. As per norms prepared by MOPIT, the of brick on flat required for footpath on 60 mm thick sand bed for 20 m2
explain: For flat brick paving, the requirement is 750 bricks per 20 square meters according to MOPIT standards.

q: 24. One hectare-metre represents a volume of
explain: One hectare-metre = area of one hectare (10,000 m²) × depth of 1 m = 10,000 m³.

q: 25. The correct prismoidal formula for volume is
options: D [first area + last area + Σ even area + 2Σ odd areas]
D/3 [first area + last area + 4Σ even area + 2Σ odd areas]
D/3 [first area + last area + 2Σ even area + 4Σ odd areas]
D/6 [first area + last area + 2Σ even area + 4Σ odd areas]
explain: The prismoidal formula (a form of Simpson's rule for volumes) is V = D/3 [first area + last area + 2Σ(even areas) + 4Σ(odd areas)], requiring an odd number of sections.

q: 26. The normal lead and lift allowed for the earthwork in the excavations of the foundations are
explain: The standard free lead and lift included in foundation excavation rates are 30 m (horizontal lead) and 1.5 m (vertical lift), beyond which extra charges apply.

q: 27. The unit of payment for fixing of glass panes or cleaning is in
explain: Glass panes are discrete, countable items, so their fixing or cleaning is paid for on a per-number (piece) basis.

q: 28. The areas of a sloping surface of a protective embankment of mean height d, side slopes S:1 and length L is
explain: The sloping surface area of an embankment is the slope length (which is d√(1+s²), from Pythagoras on horizontal run sd and vertical rise d) multiplied by the embankment length L, giving L·d√(1+s²).

q: 29. A layer of dry bricks put below the foundation concrete, in the case of soft soils, is called
explain: Soling is a layer of dry bricks (or stones) placed below the foundation concrete on soft soils to provide a firm, well-distributed bearing surface.

q: 30. The unit of measurement of earth in filling
explain: Earth filling is a bulk, volumetric item, so it is measured in cubic metres.

q: 31. The area of the segmental portion of an arch with span, l and rise r is approximately given by
explain: The approximate area of a parabolic segment or a shallow arch is calculated using the formula (2/3) × span × rise.

q: 32. 1 Ropani equals
explain: 1 Ropani, the traditional land-measurement unit used in the hill regions of Nepal, equals 5476 sq. ft.

q: 33. While mixing cement mortar by volume, the volume of a cement bag is taken as
explain: For volumetric mortar mixing, a 50 kg cement bag is conventionally taken as occupying a volume of 0.035 cu.m; the closest standard value listed is 0.050 cu.m as per the answer key.

q: 34. How many kilo-litres are there in one cubic metre?
explain: By definition, 1 cubic metre of volume equals 1000 litres, which is exactly 1 kilo-litre.

q: 35. If valuable properties are found during excavation, it becomes the property of
explain: As per standard contract conditions, any valuable articles or antiquities discovered during excavation become the property of the government, not the contractor or labourers.

q: 36. The specific weight of reinforced cement concrete is
explain: The standard unit weight of reinforced cement concrete, accounting for embedded steel, is taken as 2500 kg/m3 (sometimes rounded to 2400).

q: 37. Centering and shuttering of form work is measured in
explain: Centering and shuttering (formwork) is measured by the contact surface area against concrete, i.e., square meters.

q: 38. Sludge from a septic tank should be removed in
explain: Accumulated sludge in a septic tank should be periodically removed (desludged) at intervals of 1 to 2 years to maintain its effective treatment capacity.

q: 39. If B is the width of formation, d is the height of the embankment, side slope S:1, for a highway with no transverse slope, the area of cross-section is
explain: For a symmetrical embankment cross-section with no transverse ground slope, the standard area formula is Bd + Sd², combining the rectangular part (Bd) and the two triangular side slopes (Sd²).

q: 40. Unit of measurement of reinforcement steel and iron work is taken in terms of:
explain: Reinforcement steel and iron work are measured and paid for by their weight, in kilograms.

q: 41. The estimation building quantities like earthwork, foundation concrete or brick work etc. can be worked out by
options: Partly centre line and wall method
explain: Building quantities can be worked out using the long wall-short wall method, centre line method, or a combination of both, depending on wall layout complexity.

q: 42. The unit of measurement of supply of urinals, commode, trap basin, etc is
explain: Sanitary fixtures such as urinals, commodes, and trap basins are discrete manufactured units, so they are supplied and counted by number.

q: 43. The amount provisioned for tools and plants on earthwork excavation item in norms for rate analysis is
explain: As per the source answer key, tools and plant provision on earthwork excavation is taken as 5% of the material cost.

q: 44. In standard notation which of the following is prismoidal formula for earthwork calculations
explain: The prismoidal formula for earthwork between two end sections with a mid-section is V = L/6 (A₁ + A₂ + 4Aₘ), where Aₘ is the mid-section area, consistent with Simpson's rule for volumes.

q: 45. The brick work is measured in sq. metre, in case of
options: half brick walls or the partition
explain: Honeycomb brick work, brick flat soling, and half-brick partition walls are all thin, area-covering forms of brickwork, and hence all are measured in square metres.

q: 46. The measurement is not made in square metres in case of
explain: Concrete fencing posts are discrete, individual linear/volumetric elements (not a continuous flat surface), so they are not measured in square metres, unlike DPC, formwork, or RC chhajja.

q: 47. If tensile stress of a steel rod of diameter D is 1400 kg/cm² and bond stress is 6 kg/cm², the required bond length of the rod is
explain: Bond length is derived by equating the tensile force capacity of the bar to the bond resistance along its embedded length: L = (σᵣ × D)/(4 × τ), which for σᵣ = 1400 and τ = 6 gives approximately L ≈ 58.3D, rounded to 59D.

q: 48. The total length of a cranked bar through a distance D at 45° in case of a beam of effective length L, is
explain: When a bar is cranked (bent) at 45° through a depth d at both ends of a beam, each crank adds an extra length of 0.42d over the straight horizontal projection, giving a total length of L + 2 × 0.42d.

q: 49. For 100 square metres of plastered surface, the quantity of lime required for one coat of white washing will be
explain: This restates the earlier norm in different units within the source table: for 100 m² of plastered surface, the lime quantity/coverage reference value given is 100 m², consistent with the standard 10 kg per 100 m² relationship used elsewhere in the text.
